title_ar: الشيخ الددو يزور مركز "السلام عليك أيها النبي" بمكة
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Visits the "Peace Be upon You, O Prophet" Centre in Mecca
body_ar: قام الشيخ بزيارة مركز " السلام عليك أيها النبي" في مكة المكرمة، وقد أثار إعجاب الشيخ ما رآه من جهود مميزة لنشر سيرة المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأنشد القصيدة التالية: ( القصيدة)، ونشير هنا إلى أن هذا المركز يرأسه فضيلة الشيخ ناصر بن مسفر الزهراني ، ومقره بمكة، ويهتم بالتعريف بآثار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويسعى لتقديمها في ثوب جديد أسلوبا ومنهجا. النور شعشع في ذرى أُمِّ القُرى و ( النَّصْرُ أَسْفَر مُزْهِرَا ) وَمُنَوِّرَا ذا ( ناصر ) العلم الشريف قد انشرَا ما قد أَمَاتَ الجَهْلُ منه وأَقبَرَا من زار مركزهُ " السلام عليك يا خير الورى " سيرى به خير الورى فيرى به أنوار أحمدَ أخجَلت في الكون مفتوقَ الصباحِ الأَزهَرَا وعبير سيرته المعَطر مخجِلاً عطر الورى لو كان مِسْكًا أذْفرَا ويراهُ في كل المشاهد مُعْلمًا بالمعجزاتِ مُؤيَّدًا ومُظفَرَا ويراه في الشعب الحزين مشمرًا ويراه يخلو للعبادة في حِرَا ويراه وقت الوحي بعد نزوله في بيته مُزَّمِلاً مُدَّثِرَا ويراه يخترق الطباق مُكرَّمًا في ليلة المعراج منه والسُّرى في بيعة الرضوان يبصر صحبه مستلئمين وحين يفتح خيبرَا ويرى سيوف المصطفى وسهامه ورماحه ودروعه والمغفرَا ولباسه وفراشَهُ وأَثَاثَه وسريرَهُ وحذاءَهُ والمنبرَا وطعامه وشرابه وكتابَه ُ والخاتم المنقوش فيه مُدَوَّرَا كلٌّ يراهُ مجسَّدًا ومُمَثَّلاً تمثيلَ صِدْقٍ بارزا ومصوَّرا ويرى به ( موسوعة ) حَوَتِ الذي في الكتب ( كلُّ الصيد في جَوْفِ الفَرَى ) ( موسوعة ) حوَتِ الحديث مُخَرَّجًا حَوَتِ الكتابَ مُرَتَّلاً ومُفَسَّرَا حوتِ الشمائل والمغازي والسَّرَا يَا والبعوث وكُلُّ ما فيها جرى فيخال أن قد عاش بين صحابه دهرًا به سمع الحديث وأَبْصَرَا ويخال خيل الله بين يديه قد صبرت قنابلها تثير العِثْيَرَا فيقول مَا الأفلامُ والآثار وال قِصص المثيرة إذْ تُرَى إلا رُؤى عَجْلَى تُعَالِج عنصرًا فَرْدًا وأغلبها حديث مفترى لكن ما هُديَ الشريفُ لجمعه ونظامِهِ أو مَا لَه مِنه انْبَرى تفسيرُ صدقٍ للعناصر كلها يجلو الحقيقة لا يغادر عنصرا لله دَرُّ شريفنا ورفاقه ما أصدق الأقوامَ بل ما أصبرا قد أبدعوا ما أودعوا وأتوا بما يَسْترخصُ المغلون فيه الجوهرا يا رب فانصر ( ناصرا ) وأعزَّه وافتح له يا رب فتحًا أكبرا وقه شرور الحاسدين ورُدَّهُمْ مستسلمين إذا رأوه القهقرى وأدم صلاتك والسلام على الذي شرفته ورفعته أعلى الذرى
body_en:
The Sheikh visited the "Peace be upon you, O Prophet" Centre in Mecca the Ennobled. What he saw there of distinguished efforts to spread the biography (sīrah) of the Chosen One — may God bless him and grant him peace — stirred his admiration, and he recited the following poem: (the poem). We note here that this centre is headed by his eminence Sheikh Nasir ibn Musfir al-Zahrani, that it is based in Mecca, that it is concerned with making the relics of the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — known, and that it seeks to present them in a new dress, in style and in method.

*The light has blazed upon the heights of the Mother of Cities, and (victory has broken, blossoming) and illuminating. Here is (Nasir), he of noble learning, who has brought back to life what ignorance had killed of it and buried away. Whoever visits his centre — "Peace be upon you, O best of creation" — will see in it the best of creation. There he will see the lights of Ahmad, which have shamed, in all the cosmos, the cleaving of the radiant dawn; and the perfume of his life, fragrant, shaming the scent of all creation were that the most pungent musk. He will see him in every scene, marked out by miracles, divinely upheld and given victory. He will see him in the sorrowful ravine, girded for hardship, and see him withdrawing alone for worship in Hira. He will see him at the hour of revelation, after it came down upon him, in his house wrapped in his cloak, enveloped in his mantle. He will see him piercing the layered heavens, honoured, on the night of the Ascent (miʿrāj) and the Night Journey. At the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bayʿat al-riḍwān) he beholds his Companions clad in their mail, and beholds him when he conquers Khaybar. He sees the swords of the Chosen One and his arrows, his spears, his coats of mail and his helmet; his garment, his bedding and his furnishings, his bedstead, his sandal and the pulpit; his food, his drink and his writing, and the seal engraved upon it, round. All of it he sees embodied and represented — a truthful representation — standing out and depicted. And he sees in it (an encyclopaedia) that has gathered what lies in the books — (all the game is in the belly of the wild ass). (An encyclopaedia) that has gathered hadith with its sources traced, that has gathered the Book recited in measure and expounded; that has gathered the Prophet's traits (shamāʾil), the campaigns (maghāzī), the raiding parties (sarāyā) and the expeditions, and all that took place in them. So he fancies that he has lived among his Companions an age, hearing the hadith in it and seeing. And he fancies the horses of God before him, their squadrons standing firm, raising the dust. And he says: what are the films, the relics and the stirring tales, when they are seen, but hurried glimpses that handle one single element — and most of them a fabricated report. But that which al-Sharif has been guided to gather and to order, or what has come forth from him of it, is a truthful exposition of all the elements, one that makes the truth plain and leaves no element out. How excellent is our Sharif and his comrades! How truthful are these folk — indeed, how patient! They have made new what they laid down, and brought that beside which those who prize it would count a jewel cheap. O Lord, grant victory to (Nasir) and honour him, and open for him, O Lord, a greater opening; and guard him from the evils of the envious, and turn them back in surrender, retreating, when they see him. And continue Your blessing and Your peace upon him whom You have ennobled and raised to the highest summits.*

flags.context: the sentence introducing the poem in the news paragraph
options: translate the placeholder visibly as '(the poem)' and flag it
replace it with the poem that follows
flags.note: '( القصيدة)' is an unreplaced editorial placeholder left in the published CMS record — the editor meant to drop the poem in at that point and instead appended it below. Source defect under style guide section 11; translated visibly rather than silently removed.

flags.arabic: حوتِ الشمائل والمغازي والسَّرَا يَا والبعوث ... فيقول مَا الأفلامُ والآثار وال قِصص المثيرة
flags.context: two places in the qasida where a word is split in two
options: leave the split visible in body_ar and translate the intended word
flags.note: The poem was published in a two-column HTML table and the CMS text extraction flattens it. Two words are broken across the column boundary: 'والسَّرَا يَا' for 'والسرايا' (the raiding parties) and 'وال قِصص' for 'والقصص' (and the tales). The split is left visible in body_ar; the English translates the evidently intended word. 678 tatweel (U+0640) elongation characters, pure typographic padding from the same table, were removed from body_ar — this is declared normalisation, not a silent fix.

flags.arabic: لكن ما هُديَ الشريفُ لجمعه ... لله دَرُّ شريفنا ورفاقه
flags.context: the two verses praising the compiler of the centre's work
options: read al-Sharif as the title of a named individual and leave it untranslated as a name
read it as the adjective 'the noble one'
read it as a reference to Sheikh Nasir ibn Musfir al-Zahrani himself
flags.note: 'الشريف' appears twice as an apparent title or name distinct from 'ناصر', who is named separately in the same poem. The prose names only Nasir ibn Musfir al-Zahrani as head of the centre, so the referent of al-Sharif is not resolvable from the record. Left as a title in the English. Needs the Sheikh's office to identify the person.

flags.context: the parenthesis in the opening verse
options: a quoted phrase or motto set off by the poet
a chronogram giving a date in abjad numerals
flags.note: The poem sets several phrases in parentheses — this one, '( ناصر )', '( موسوعة )' and the proverb '( كلُّ الصيد في جَوْفِ الفَرَى )'. The others are clearly the poet marking a name or a quoted proverb; this one is not self-explanatory and may be a chronogram. Rendered literally. Note also that the proverb is spelled 'الفرى' where the standard form is 'الفرا'; left as served.

translator_notes: The poem is the Sheikh's own composition, recited on the visit, so it is primary material and not a routine news notice; it is typed 'news' only because the record structure offers no better value for a news report that carries a text.
Rendered as prose in italics per style guide section 4; no attempt at rhymed English. The Arabic is retained in full in body_ar for the bilingual pane.
'الفرى' in the proverb, and the divided words, are left as the source has them.
